subject: Private VPC boundary stitching proposal and ops annotation review
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: EdgeCloud Solutions <eng@edgecloud.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC boundary stitching proposal and ops annotation review

Team / EdgeCloud,

Attaching two reference diagrams for the Private VPC deployment (control plane & data plane stitching). Goal: validate the "stitching" approach where the control plane is called across a dedicated interconnect while the data plane egress is proxied through tenant-specific sidecars. Key asks: please review port ranges, MTU assumptions, failover behavior, and the certificate rotation boundary.

Summary of proposed pattern (high level):
- Control plane: dedicated peered VRF over the customer interconnect; control plane traffic kept on a management CIDR, mTLS to Redwood CA; BGP session for reachability on put/data plane attach.
- Data plane: per-tenant sidecar proxies in the colocations; egress via tenant NAT with prefix-based exclusions for telemetry; ephemeral outbound NAT for non-sensitive traffic.
- Boundary stitching: an HA proxy pair in the colocation handles ingress for model traffic and forwards to Redis/KV cache over the management fabric using route-target tagging.
- Fallback: when interconnect degraded, traffic should failover to an encrypted tunnel (GRE + IPsec) over a secondary provider link.

Attachments: diagram_A_zone_mapping.pdf (zone/CIDR mapping), diagram_B_proxy_chaining.png (proxy chaining + sequencing).

Open questions for EdgeCloud:
1) Do you have constraints on maximum MTU over the interconnect (we assumed 9000)?
2) Are there BGP community recommendations for our route-targeting?
3) For the fallback tunnel, any preferences (GRE vs VXLAN) based on existing colo fabric?
4) Ops: how would you instrument health for control-plane RPC vs data egress differences?

Please reply with inline comments or drop edits onto the Drive link. Hoping to finalize a single-sheet runbook + canary playbook by next Wed so engineering can schedule the cutover.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: diagram_A_zone_mapping.pdf (95KB), diagram_B_proxy_chaining.png (1.2MB)

Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC boundary stitching proposal and ops annotation review

Markus — thanks for the clear summary and diagrams. Attached a quick markup with suggested changes (edgecloud_suggested_changes.v1.png). High level notes: 

- MTU: our fabric supports 9216 on the dedicated interconnect but the provider handoff often reduces to 9000; plan for 9000 + path-MTU checks.
- BGP: prefer to use extended communities for tenant tagging rather than route-targets on the fabric; this avoids accidental leak to shared services. We can share a template community set if helpful.
- Fallback: we generally recommend IPsec over GRE for the secondary path due to hardware offload on our platform; VXLAN adds complexity unless you need L2 adjacency.
- NAT exclusions: suggest an explicit exclusion list for telemetry and KV cache control IPs to avoid double-NAT and TTL issues (see markup).
- Certificates: rotation inside the colo should use an intermediate cert signed by Redwood CA; we can accept OCSP stapling if Redwood exposes OCSP endpoints over the interconnect.

Operationally, we'll want health checks split into: (a) control-plane RPC latency + auth checks, (b) sidecar egress success rate, (c) BGP adjacency and route consistency. We can expose SNMP traps or push to your Prometheus remote write; happy to wire either.

Attaching: edgecloud_suggested_changes.v1.png (480KB) — inline comments on the PDF.

Subject: Re: Private VPC boundary stitching proposal and ops annotation review

Thanks Sarah, Markus — good recs. A couple security/ops items from my side: 

- KMS / cert rotation: we need proof of key separation for intermediate certs in colo (HSM-backed preferred). Can EdgeCloud provide an artifact showing where the private keys are held and who has administrative access?
- Telemetry exclusion list: strongly agree — telemetry and KV cache control plane must be excluded from NAT and should traverse the management fabric only. We should list exact IPs and a small port set (6379 for redis, 443 for control RPC, 22 for jump hosts if needed).
- MTU/path-MTU checks: add an explicit pre-cutover test in the runbook that runs ICMP MTU probes and verifies MSS adjustments for TCP flows.
- Canary: propose a staged canary where we route 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72 hours with automated rollback on error rate > 0.8%. I drafted a short playbook (canary_playbook.md).

Thanks everyone — consolidating decisions and owners below so we can lock the runbook and schedule the cutover window. Please flag anything I missed.

Decisions: 
- MTU baseline: 9000; confirm path-MTU test in staging and production (owner: Priyom, due: 2028-04-21).
- BGP tagging: use extended communities template from EdgeCloud (owner: Sarah / EdgeCloud to share template by 2028-04-19).
- Fallback: IPsec over GRE recommended by EdgeCloud (owner: Priyom to validate hardware offload support by 2028-04-22).
- Telemetry & KV exclusions: hard-coded exclusion list to be added to runbook; Kimberly to provide final IP/port list by 2028-04-20.
- Canary rollout: use staged percentages over 72 hours with automatic rollback; Marissa to own canary orchestration (playbook link below).
- Cert rotation: intermediate certs in colo must be HSM-backed or explicit justification provided; EdgeCloud to provide key custody artifact (Sarah, due: 2028-04-19).

Action items & owners:
- Priyom Das: run MTU/probe tests in staging and report (2028-04-21) — PRIY-TEST-001.
- Sarah Lim / EdgeCloud: share extended community templates + key custody artifact (2028-04-19).
- Kimberly Park: finalize telemetry exclusion list and KMS requirements (2028-04-20).
- Marissa Cole: prepare canary orchestration and pipeline; wire Prometheus remote-write (2028-04-23).
- Markus: publish final one-pager + drive folder and propose cutover window (2028-04-24).

Links: drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDE_example_diagrams — I've added an annotated runbook draft.
Jira ticket: NETOPS-1248 (I'll add sub-tasks).
Canary playbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/runbooks/canary-rollout

Next meeting: quick 30-min sync Thursday 2028-04-20 09:00 PT to confirm artifacts and SLA items.

Thanks — will follow up with the final PDF runbook after the meeting.

-Markus
